| SA-160 | `dsm_sdk/build.rs` · `main` | dsm_sdk build.rs release guard checks CARGO_FEATURE_test, which Cargo never sets, so it never fires. | confirmed (1 of 1) | Fixed (`558af6d3`) |

**The changes.** Every fix below has a test that performs the attack and goes red with the fix removed; each mutation was applied in place on a committed tree, its named test run on the release build, and the file restored byte for byte (`git diff` empty afterwards).

- **SA-64.** `recovery.enable`, `recovery.cacheMnemonic` and `recovery.createCapsule` wrote the given phrase's seed over the wallet seed, in memory and sealed, re-rooting the identity and the app lock's phrase. The recovery routes now cache only K_R and the recovery authority keypair (`RecoverySDK::cache_recovery_keys`), and `enable` and `createCapsule` refuse a phrase whose seed does not derive this identity's AK (`require_this_wallets_phrase`, the check cold-start init makes). The NFC screen's "Generate new mnemonic" flow and `recovery.generateMnemonic` are removed: a backup is armed with the wallet's own phrase. Test: `ingress::tests::no_recovery_route_replaces_the_wallet_seed`. Mutations: the phrase check reduced to a length comparison, and `cacheMnemonic` calling `derive_and_cache_key` again, each red.
- **SA-65.** `recovery.disable` ran the logout wipe and deleted the wallet's only sealed seed. It now clears the recovery keys only (`clear_recovery_keys`); `delete_encrypted_wallet_seed` had no other caller and is removed. Test: `ingress::tests::disabling_backup_keeps_the_wallet_seed`. Mutation: the seed cache cleared beside the keys, red.
- **SA-118.** The K_R blob builds before SA-17's fix wrapped under public values is deleted whenever the recovery tables open.
- **SA-66.** A finality certificate naming no journal, or a transition this device already finalized, and a countersign delta naming a finalized proposal, consumed the message id they were read under with no signature checked. Only a certificate or delta this device verified and applied consumes its id; the rest are passed over by their content (`take_in_finality_certificate`, `take_in_countersign_delta`). Test: `handlers::storage_routes::tests::only_a_verified_artifact_consumes_the_id_it_was_read_under`. Mutation: a `NoJournal` certificate consuming its id, red.
- **SA-68.** The paged cell read had no bound on pages. A page a member ends short of `MAX_CELL_PAGE_ENTRIES` must be borne out by the next page's first value, which must not have fit, and one member's whole cell read has one transport deadline (`CELL_READ_DEADLINE`, a liveness bound like `MEMBER_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, never a verdict). Tests: `sdk::storage_node_sdk::tests::a_member_cutting_every_page_short_is_not_answering`, `a_cell_read_ends_at_its_deadline_however_slow_the_pages`, and `a_page_ended_short_by_the_value_after_it_is_read_on` (an honest short page is read on). Mutations: the short-page check disabled, and the deadline multiplied a thousandfold, each red.
- **SA-70.** A faucet release frozen at a reserve head for an earlier position was reused at a later one. The claim reuses a frozen release only when it names the claim's target position, and otherwise signs and freezes its own (`freeze_release`). Test: `handlers::faucet_flow_tests::a_release_frozen_for_an_earlier_position_is_not_reused_at_a_later_one`. Mutation: any frozen release reused, red.
- **SA-84.** A Close or Release whose single core names a vault other than B°'s is refuted from the operation alone (`SettlementCoreReferenceMismatch { field: "B°.dlv_core.vault_id" }`). Test: `sofi::validation::tests::a_close_whose_core_names_another_vault_is_invalid_in_hand`. Mutation: the vault id compared with itself, red.
- **SA-115.** The proposer's `Prepared` phase is written over the `Preparing` phase it was decided on (`record_prepared`), so a cancellation made while the prepare was built stands. Test: `bluetooth::bilateral_ble_handler::tests::a_proposal_cancelled_while_its_prepare_was_built_stays_cancelled`. Mutation: the unconditional write restored, red.
- **SA-119, SA-120.** The Core bridge's recovery arms (a capsule decrypted under a key the request carried and staged, and a tombstone, succession and resume run around the router's gates) and its `nfc:recovery` external commit are removed with the handler registry; recovery runs only as the router's `recovery.*` routes. Nothing sent those operations. The router's `recovery.decryptCapsule` now stages the capsule's source device and genesis, which only the removed path staged and the tombstone reads. Tests: `core::bridge::tests::no_recovery_operation_runs_through_the_bridge`, `ingress::tests::decrypting_a_ring_capsule_stages_the_device_it_was_sealed_by`. The path no longer exists, so there is no gate to mutate.
- **SA-125.** Approving the same connect code again keeps the highest request its session took. Test: `storage::client_db::connect::tests::approving_a_code_again_keeps_the_requests_its_session_took`. Mutation: the lower of the two kept, red.
- **SA-146.** The next cert-resync epoch is a checked add (`next_resync_epoch`); a contact that pushed the epoch to `i64::MAX` breaks only its own relationship. Test: `storage::client_db::cert_resync::tests::a_relationship_whose_epochs_are_spent_cannot_be_resynced_and_panics_nothing`. Mutation: the unchecked `+ 1` restored, red (it panics).
- **SA-107, SA-155.** Every third-party action in every workflow runs by commit (89 pins, the version in the comment beside each); cargo-audit, cargo-ndk and cargo-cyclonedx install at exact versions, cargo-audit no longer behind `|| true`; elan's installer is fetched at v4.2.4's commit and checked against its digest. `ci/check_toolchain_consistency.sh` reads the Rust version from the pinned action's comment and passes.
- **SA-154.** The Gradle distribution is pinned by `distributionSha256Sum`, and CI checks the committed wrapper jar against Gradle 8.14.5's published digest with no network.
- **SA-151.** GCP nodes on the `default` network deny SSH and RDP from anywhere at priority 1000, ahead of the default allow rules; SSH from `allowed_ssh_cidr` is allowed at 900. Not applied to the fleet: `terraform apply` is the operator's.
- **SA-153.** The receipt rate counts Gmail addresses without the dots Gmail ignores, at both its domains. Test: `tests::only_a_bare_address_is_a_recipient_and_its_spellings_count_as_one`. Mutation: Gmail folding removed, red.
- **SA-156.** Report and feedback links carry no diagnostics.
- **SA-157.** What a connected application chose is shown without bidi controls or invisible characters. Test: `AppsScreen.linkOrigin.test.tsx` "shows the application its name and summary with no bidi override". Mutation: the filter made the identity, red.
- **SA-90.** A failed advance with no admission plan cleared the head's pending admission, which it had not made, so the next admission could take the same position. Only an attach the advance made itself is rolled off. Test: `handlers::faucet_flow_tests::a_failed_advance_keeps_the_pending_admission_it_did_not_make`. Mutation: the admission cleared on every failure, red.
- **SA-111.** `bilateral.pending_list` refused the whole list for one stored session that was not a transfer. It lists transfers and passes over other steps. Test: `bluetooth::bilateral_ble_handler::tests::the_pending_list_passes_over_a_step_that_is_not_a_transfer`. Mutation: the pass-over removed, red.
- **SA-160.** `dsm_sdk/build.rs` checked `CARGO_FEATURE_test`, which no feature sets, so it never fired. It is removed rather than kept as a gate guarding nothing.
- **SA-108.** While the page holds a screen guard, `WalletWebView` drops a touch that came while any part of its window was covered (`ScreenGuards.dropsTouch`). Test: `ScreenGuardsTest.a_partly_covered_window_takes_no_touch_while_a_guard_is_held`. Mutation: the partial rule disabled, red.

- **SA-131.** A Close or Release whose vault core names another trader, and a fold entry whose core advances from another relationship base, were taken. The core's trader must be `P`'s, and each entry's base the core's own (`validation.rs`). Tests: `a_vault_core_advancing_from_another_base_is_invalid`, `a_close_whose_vault_core_names_another_trader_is_invalid`. Mutations: the base check removed, and the whole trader condition removed from Close, each red. Release carries the same trader check; it is not mutation-proven separately.
- **SA-86.** An exercise whose `F` named a vault its `P` has no leg for made the relay refuse the whole exercise, so the vault's key stayed held for good. The relay passes over that attempt and carries the legs `P` has (`leg_cells`). Test: `handlers::node_e2e_tests::an_exercise_naming_a_vault_its_precommit_has_no_leg_for_does_not_freeze_the_vault`. Mutation: the refusal restored, red.
- **SA-72.** A key held short of final by an exercise whose pair is already registered, lost or misbodied was stepped past, so the trader drafted on an attempt whose skip could not conform until someone else finished the key. The walk carries the exercise to its keys (`carry_held_exercise`, which writes nothing at the pair) and walks again once the key is final. Test: `handlers::node_e2e_tests::a_held_key_whose_pair_is_registered_is_carried_to_final_before_the_walk_goes_on`. Mutation: the carry removed, red.
- **SA-73.** The recovery re-establish accept-guard ran on the unsigned header's device id before the contact lookup and Core's decision on the prepare. It runs only on a prepare Core decided from the sender's pinned identity and signature. Test: `bluetooth::bilateral_ble_handler::tests::a_recovery_prepare_from_a_stranger_is_refused_before_the_guard_runs`. Mutation: the guard moved back before the decision, red.
- **SA-121.** The guard took the recovery authority from the claimed successor's own head and anchor. The authority is the one the tombstoned predecessor anchored, read under the genesis this device pinned for it (`predecessor_anchoring`, `succession_proof_anchored_by_predecessor`). Test: `handlers::node_e2e_tests::a_succession_proof_counts_only_under_the_authority_its_predecessor_anchored`. Mutation: the successor's own anchor checked instead, red.
- **SA-117, the verifier correction the owner approved.** Tombstones are signed under K_A and were verified under the old device's AK, so none was ever taken in. The notice now carries the tombstone with its authority and succession, and a contact verifies it under the authority the tombstoned device anchored. The pipeline stored only the succession's signature as its receipt and only warned when the store failed; it stores the receipt and fails on error. Test: `handlers::node_e2e_tests::a_tombstone_is_taken_in_under_the_authority_the_device_anchored`. Mutation: verification under the contact's AK restored, red. Not done: nothing yet consults the tombstone record (`is_device_tombstoned` has no caller), so a retired device's messages are not refused. The owner approved the verifier correction only.
- **SA-95, in part.** A conditional claim's predecessor offered both of its roots as parents, so a claim written also along the other root's cell (anyone may write it) read as a fork. Only the root the claim names (its void root, P15-2) is offered (`parents_of_conditional`). Test: `economic::peer_lineage::tests::a_conditional_claim_copied_along_its_parents_other_root_is_no_fork`. Mutation: both roots offered, red. Not done: the owner's condition, "a conditional predecessor yields only its selected root". Resolving `q − 1` from the root its own `P` names, inside the lookup of `q` (`cc1f7ca5`), re-entered the vault walk without end: `a_reader_at_a_baseline_proves_roots_below_it_from_the_vaults_history` overflows its stack with that commit and passes without it (checked by building both). It is reverted (`60ad7fb6`). Resolving `q − 1` through its own parent reads past one position back, which DSM Amendment A14 excludes ("Nothing at n − 2 is read"). Until this is decided, a peer that builds on the root its conditional predecessor did not select is not refused at acceptance; the same holds for a single-root step after a conditional position. The test went with `parents_of_conditional` under A19 (§6.90).
- **SA-83.** A key held by an exercise whose pair was lost (or whose trader parent or Release verdict rules it out) stayed unclassified for good when another leg's liveness walk ran past `CHAIN_DEPTH`. The facts that stand on the walked key alone (`establish_key_ground`) decide a skip before the other legs are read. Test: `sofi::facts::tests::a_key_whose_pair_is_lost_is_dead_before_the_other_legs_are_read`. Mutation: the key-only facts made to need every leg, red. The wiring in `facts_of` is covered by that test and the existing walk suites; it is not mutation-proven separately.
- **SA-92, in part.** The process kept every peer verdict Core gave for its whole life (`ValidatedPeers`), while A14 refuses a position once a second claim is final there from another parent. The process memo is removed. Final cells and objects stay kept as evidence (`final_reads`), and one SoFi operation's contexts keep the answers they were given for that operation only (`ReadOnce`). Without that, a vault walk's nested resolutions re-ran each other until the stack overflowed. A holdings status checks the root one hop on every poll. Test: `handlers::one_hop_verification_tests::a_step_validated_before_its_position_forked_is_refused_after`. Mutation: a process memo restored in `resolve_peer`, red. Not done: the persisted vault-chain rows the row also names are unchanged. The test went with A14's fork refusal under A19 (§6.90).
- **SA-110.** A signed rejection did not name the device it answered, so a contact that sent another contact's commitment could relay the rejection it got and end that contact's proposal. The rejection names its addressee, and a proposer takes only one addressed to itself. Tests: `a_rejection_verifies_only_as_its_rejector_signed_it` and `a_proposal_is_abandoned_only_for_a_rejection_its_counterparty_signed`, each with an addressed-elsewhere case. Mutation: the addressee left out of the signed message, red.
- **SA-114.** An old proposal delivered after the relationship moved past its tip was kept as the sender's observed tip, which tripped the divergence check for good. Each tip a relationship moves past is recorded where it moves (`relationship_passed_tips`, written by a step's commit and a tip sync's advance), and a claimed tip on that record is not kept. Test: `bluetooth::offline_step_tests::an_old_proposal_delivered_after_the_tip_moved_is_not_kept_as_the_senders_tip`. Mutation: the record write removed, red. The table is created on open, with no schema bump; tips passed before this build are not on it.
- **SA-98.** The route writer carried any arrival record a seat returned, so one seat's false record made every later link invalid. A record counts as a link only when the seat's own log gives it for the copy (`copy_record`, `borne_out`); any other is recorded as an empty. Test: `sdk::route_seats::tests::a_seat_lying_about_its_record_is_recorded_empty_and_the_value_is_final`. Mutation: any returned record accepted, red.
- **SA-142.** `select_entry` proved every value read, duplicates and junk included, before it compared counters. Each distinct encoding is now proven once, best first, and the choice stops at the first that proves itself (`select_proven`). Test: `core::identity::directory::tests::each_distinct_entry_is_proven_once_and_the_best_that_proves_itself_stops_the_choice` (four proofs, not eight). Mutation: every value proven, red.
- **SA-124.** Connect's `AcceptIssued` rooted (adopted) the anchor and checked its creator afterwards, so a request under the grant left another device's object adopted after the refusal. The creator is read from the committed policy first (`verified_policy`, which stores nothing). Test: `handlers::connect_e2e_tests::an_object_another_device_created_is_never_adopted_for_an_application`. Mutation: rooting before the check, red.
- **SA-129.** Declining a hand-approved request whose run had committed its payment and failed to record it recorded a refusal over the payment. Decline reads what the request committed first (`finish_committed`, as Approve does). Test: `handlers::connect_e2e_tests::declining_a_request_its_crashed_run_carried_out_records_it_carried_out`. Mutation: the read skipped, red.
- **SA-98's cost.** The writer reads each later seat's log once per write, one more round trip per seat. `a_faucet_claim_reads_the_cell_it_won_once` counts them (15 reads over 5 seats).
- **SA-61, the owner's ruling (2026-10-18): "Disable the vulnerable acceptance path until the complete proof is implemented."** Core's `decide_prepare` refuses an offline-bearer transfer addressed to this device on its operation alone, before any key, signature or tip is consulted and before anything is written; the receiver's bearer-confirm machinery stays, unreached, for the complete proof (owner's choice, 2026-10-18: "Disable offline bearer receipt by refusing bearer transfers at the receiver's prepare in Core, keep the bearer-confirm machinery dormant for the complete proof, and convert the bearer tests to assert the refusal"). The six bearer tests in `offline_step_tests` assert the refusal instead: the terms checks still run first; the receiver holds and is credited nothing; a redelivery is refused again; the sender's appliance spends no counter step and the relationship takes its next step; a recovering sender cannot propose; the receiver never pins the sender's anchor. The receipt-rule and release-acceptance checks those tests ran end to end (SA-54's release gate among them) are no longer exercised through a receiver. Tests: `bilateral::offline::tests::a_bearer_transfer_addressed_here_is_refused_on_its_operation_alone`, `bluetooth::offline_step_tests::a_bearer_transfer_is_refused_at_its_receiver_and_credits_nothing`. Mutation: the refusal removed, each red. Still open: the proof itself (§52/§67's predicate at the receiver), which is what re-enables receipt.

- **The offline account, the owner's design (2026-10-19).** The owner rejected disabling as the end state (2026-10-18: "I asked you to fix fucking things, not disable them") and set the design: the offline account "was never supposed to be the same tree as the online one ... You're transferring it to a whole different SMT with a subroot"; "It's like a smaller SMT coming off the bigger one"; "it still needs the counter leaf as well"; "the Tropics Monotonic is the hardware version of the software. The software is the authority"; the receiver attests to the chip as well ("why would it not attest to the chip as well?"); and the software uptick and the hardware counter move "in one motion so that if it cancels, neither works. It's either both succeed or both fail", the software staged first "because it can be dropped, whereas the hardware cannot", and "It either fully finishes or it doesn't at all. It resets." The owner's review the same day approved the architecture with a build order, and kept acceptance off until its last phase ("I approve the general architecture, but not re-enabling offline bearer acceptance at the end of Phase 1"): (1) canonical accounting — the account tree, admitted load and unload, funding-origin evidence, deterministic economic write sets; (2) one-motion spends, full receiver proofs, durable crash recovery and SA-91's pending-credit reconciliation, proven on the host appliance; (3) hardware persistence and provisioning; (4) bearer acceptance. The review's recovery table governs the appliance: no durable transaction and the counter unchanged, start again; prepared and unchanged, reset (the owner's "it resets"); prepared and advanced, complete the exact recorded transition; committed and advanced, re-emit; missing or inconsistent and advanced, fail closed. `Appliance::recover` in `Status::Ready` adopts an advanced chip counter with the old root, which that last row forbids. Phase 1, first part: the account is its own SMT (`types::offline_account`) — allocation per asset, the software counter, the frontier and the funding origin — and its root is the value of one device-SMT leaf, `H(DSM/offline-account/v1 ‖ B)`; each load, unload and spend is one write set over it, and `verify_step` folds the write set recomputed from the step and its stated pre-values against the account's pre-root, so the leaves a step does not name are proven unchanged. Tests: `types::offline_account::tests::a_spend_from_an_allocation_the_account_never_held_does_not_fold`, `a_spend_moves_the_allocation_counter_and_frontier_and_nothing_else`.

- **The offline account, Phase 1: canonical accounting (2026-10-19).** The owner's authorization the same day: "Proceed with the schema-2 boundary-funded witness and finish the canonical load/unload integration", the unload's credit funded by "an equal, authenticated reduction in the offline account" and "an exactly-once consumption rule", with "a dedicated boundary-funded credit witness, not an unrestricted no-cost credit-source arm". What landed:
  - *The account is its own SMT, its root one device leaf* (`types::offline_account`; `DeviceState::offline_accounts`). Leaves: the allocation per asset, the software counter, the frontier, the funding chain. The fused anchor-state leaf and the flat allocation leaves are deleted, with their keys and tags. Every transition is one write set over the account, and `verify_step` folds it from the account's pre-root, so a leaf a step does not name is proven unchanged. An account opens once per bundle, at a chip that has never released (`u = 0`).
  - *The funding chain commits every boundary.* A boundary's identity (`OfflineBoundaryId`) hashes the device and account roots it starts from, and the account root holds the previous chain value, so the leaf is a hash chain over every load and unload since the account opened: a later load extends it and never replaces an earlier load's provenance (test `economic::offline_boundary::tests::the_funding_chain_commits_every_earlier_boundary`).
  - *Load and unload are admitted economic transitions.* The substrate is the boundary body (`0x002A` load, `0x002B` unload, promoted from reserved): the pre-roots, the account's pre-values, and the account and device paths. `OfflineBoundaryBody::verify` folds both trees from it and derives the identity and the digest; nothing about the boundary's effect is carried as a claim. A load's write set is its exact balance debit; an unload's is its exact balance credit, funded by `CreditSourceOfflineBoundaryDebit` (`0x0075`, witness schema 2, schema 1 burned), with the source — derived from the boundary's identity — consumed from zero in the same witness. `advance_validated` binds the witness to the boundary's identity and checks the exact write set; the provenance arm funds only an unload, of the body's asset and amount; `non_reuse` records the source as consumed. The peer walk validates boundary steps, and a boundary is never a debit a credit can name. An admission's coordinates keep a successor's `(C_dsm+, parent)` or, for a boundary, nothing beside its body (`AcceptedSubstrateCoords`).
  - *The SDK admits the boundary end to end* (`admitted_offline_boundary`, `CoreSDK::admitted_boundary`): Core takes the boundary from the head; the body, write set, witness and manifest are built from exactly that; the head carrying the admission, the pending row and the frozen evidence commit in one transaction under the same predecessor check every admission uses; the one finish publishes, registers, validates and admits it, and resume finishes it from the frozen body. The direct load/unload, which moved value with no canonical operation, is deleted.
  - *The chip follows the software, never the reverse.* Staging and the routes require the chip to stand at the account's counter and frontier (`require_offline_account_at`); the per-stage reconcile that rewrote the device's anchor leaf to the chip's live state is deleted. A bearer spend steps the account's counter and frontier in the same device root as its relationship leaf; its receipt proves the account leaf by a `SpendWitness`, held to the counter and frontiers its release signs; the release carries `OfflineStateProof`s that anchor-core's predicate checks through the DSM verifier (`verify_offline_state`, refusals typed `OfflineStateRefused`).
  - *Formats.* Client DB schema 32 (`bilateral_sessions.spend_next_frontier`; the pending-admission successor columns nullable by kind), device-head codec `0x08` (the offline accounts), witness schema 2. Each refuses the old format at open; nothing migrates. A device holding a pre-cut allocation must be reset — refused, not silently dropped.
  - Tests: `economic_admission_lifecycle::an_offline_load_and_unload_advance_the_lineage_and_an_unload_funds_once`, `::an_offline_debit_funds_only_an_unload_and_only_once_recorded`; `handlers::offline_boundary_tests::a_load_and_an_unload_are_admitted_and_walkable_and_an_unload_funds_once` (on the pinned set, both foreign-walked as boundaries); `handlers::offline_cash_routes::tests::the_offline_account_is_never_rewritten_to_follow_the_chip`; `types::device_state::tests::a_bearer_spend_draws_from_the_account_and_moves_its_counter_and_frontier`, `::the_receipt_of_a_bearer_spend_proves_the_account_its_release_advances`; `economic::offline_boundary::tests::*`; `types::offline_account::tests::*`. Mutation, each gate removed and its named test red, eleven of eleven: the device-root fold, the identity bound to the witness, the unload credit's amount, `0x0075` only on an unload, `0x0075` recorded as consumed, the consumed source refused at build, the counter's step, the state proof's counter, the receipt's account being the release's, the chip standing where the account does, the account opening only at the enrolled origin.
  - Still open, by the owner's phases: (2) the one-motion spend with a durable prepared transaction and the recovery table, full receiver proofs (funding ancestry walked from the account's chain, the chip-signed counter step), SA-91's pending-credit reconciliation, SA-112, SA-116; (3) hardware persistence and provisioning; (4) bearer acceptance, which stays refused until then.

**Round three (2026-10-20, `fix/security-audit-remaining-rows` into this branch).** The rows the open-next list named, as five sessions fixed them on their own branches and this branch merged them, and the storage-junk, Connect-pacing and economic-verifier rows the owner's rulings of 2026-10-18 approved. Mutations, run in place on the committed tree, are recorded in VERIFICATION_MATRIX.

- **Fixed on the sessions' branches, merged here.** SA-96, SA-105, SA-106, SA-150, SA-152 (`ac72615f`): mirrors fetch an inflated member's newest cycles at once, waits share the pool, proof builds past the queue answer busy, a cancelled close keeps its leaf set, the node's connections have a per-peer share. Tests: `dsm_storage_node::bytecommit_chain::a_member_inflated_past_one_sync_is_mirrored_at_its_newest_cycles_at_once`, `::b0x_wait::waits_starting_together_leave_the_pool_to_everyone_else`, `::proof_tree_builds::proofs_past_the_queued_tree_builds_are_answered_busy_at_once`, `db::cell_properties::a_close_whose_caller_goes_away_keeps_the_leaf_set_it_held`, `::resource_limits::one_peer_holds_no_more_than_its_share_of_the_nodes_connections`. SA-122, SA-123, SA-126 (`4895662b`): `dsm-app-host` `relay::tests::a_peer_holds_no_more_connections_than_its_share`, `::an_idle_bound_inside_the_request_time_is_refused`, `::one_peer_holds_no_more_than_its_share_of_the_relays_requests`; `handlers::connect_e2e_tests::a_read_of_requests_for_no_session_is_refused`, `::a_transfer_taken_in_while_a_request_pays_is_not_the_requests`. SA-100, SA-101, SA-109, SA-113, SA-138, SA-139 (`0b91b682`): `handlers::recipient_dispatch::tests::a_contacts_unbound_backlog_is_bounded_per_kind`, `::the_first_member_cannot_fill_a_routes_budget`, `bluetooth::gatt_identity::tests::an_identity_naming_no_contact_is_answered_at_once`, `bluetooth::ble_frame_coordinator::tests::an_address_rotating_peer_cannot_push_out_a_frame_that_is_arriving`, `sdk::inbox_poller::tests::a_contact_withholding_its_certificate_cannot_hold_the_settlement_cadence`, `sdk::inbox_waiter::tests::a_member_answering_after_the_quick_mark_cannot_skip_the_back_off`. SA-158, SA-159 (`fbf9e49c`, `029652cc`): the frontend's escrow-lock and name tests. SA-137 (`bff6ffd4`) is carried by the fold below.
- **SA-62, SA-67, SA-99: streaming recognition (storage spec §9, route chains, rule 3; the owner's ruling for storage junk).** A cell read no longer gathers a member's whole cell under an 8 MiB budget and refuses past it. A member's pages are handed to the reader as they arrive (`MemberClient::fold_cell`, page-shape checks of SA-68 kept, the transport deadline kept), and the reader keeps only what can count: Core's `HeldLog` folds every entry into the running hash and keeps only the cell's route copies its keep rule accepts, each value once (`route_chain::recognized_copies`, and each cell type's `keeps()`: root claims, reserve releases, exercises, fulfillments, verdicts naming the cell, Starts and match occupants). `record_is_committed` reads running hashes from whatever holds them (`RunningHashes`). A seat's kept copies are held to `HELD_LOG_BUDGET`; bytes that are no kept copy never count toward it. The directory, recovery and register-key reads keep only objects of their kind naming the key (`names_directory_entry`, `RecoveryCell::holds`, claims naming `K_root`). SA-99: a log read before its seat's cycle closed is read on to the entry the close committed (`HeldLog::want`), so a write landing between the read and the close no longer leaves the cell undecided. SA-62 is the reserve's instance of SA-67: the reserve's leader and named-root reads stream with the release rule (`SuccessorCell::keeps`, `named_successor_keeps`). Tests: `route_chain::tests::a_log_kept_by_what_can_count_reads_what_the_whole_log_reads`, `::each_seat_log_is_folded_once_however_many_copies_it_holds`; `sdk::storage_node_sdk::tests::junk_past_any_budget_is_read_through_to_the_value_after_it`; `sdk::route_seats::tests::junk_past_any_budget_at_the_leader_blocks_no_read`, `::a_write_between_the_read_and_the_close_leaves_the_value_final`. What remains bounded rather than free: copies of a recognized value under distinct bogus chains at a later seat count toward `HELD_LOG_BUDGET` (a resource limit, a seat not read, never a verdict). A verdict for another cell written to a verdict cell is no object naming it, and is no longer listed as passed over.
- **SA-76.** With the reads streaming, a read-ahead window holds the recognized releases of its cells, not their seats' whole logs. Partial: the window is not yet held to a byte total, and the walk's memo (SA-75) is unchanged.
- **SA-97.** One retrieval reads a member's spool pages up to one page at its largest in bytes as well as sixteen pages (`B0xSDK::reads_on`), and a sync reads its routes four at a time (`ROUTES_READ_AT_ONCE`), so what a sync holds at once is bounded by bytes, not by how many routes it has. Test: `sdk::b0x_sdk::member_answer_bounds::a_retrieval_reads_a_node_within_one_page_of_bytes`.
- **SA-136.** Core's transfer rule checks the token's committed `transferable` on every Transfer it admits or walks (`provenance::check_transfer_policy`, called in `advance_validated`), from Core's own bytes for ERA and otherwise from bytes the resolver anchors that re-hash to the commit; a policy not established keeps its class (`TransferPolicy`, Incomplete), a non-transferable token is `AssetNotTransferable`, Invalid. The never-built `MarketLegPolicy` variant and the comment that claimed a market-leg conjunct at that point are deleted: market legs are checked in SoFi validation. Test: `economic_admission_lifecycle::a_transfer_of_a_token_whose_policy_does_not_transfer_is_refused_by_core`. Open: an end-to-end walk of a hostile sender's non-transferable transfer by a third party.
- **SA-134.** An admission's finish waits only on the evidence frozen with its own manifest (`list_unpublished_frozen_with`); the device's whole table is the sweep's. Test: `handlers::frontier_verification_tests::an_admission_publishes_its_own_evidence_behind_an_older_backlog` (an object frozen for a set no catalog names no longer holds the claim).
- **SA-135 (A14: "exactly one claim may survive").** The located claim is the one final at its route only when no other candidate is undecided: a rival holding its own route's leader link short of final, or a rival whose route the reads do not decide, leaves the position not established, never the lone claim accepted. A conditional rival beside a single-root survivor is read one position back and, final, makes the two a fork. The register probe needs `members − FINAL_LINKS + 1` answers, the fewest that must include a member holding a copy of any final claim (coverage, never a vote); the fetcher reports each member's answer (`MemberAnswers`). Tests: `economic::peer_lineage::tests::a_final_claim_beside_an_undecided_rival_is_not_established`, `::a_register_probe_too_few_members_answered_establishes_nothing`. Its tests went with the register probe and the rival weighing under A19 (§6.90).
- **SA-82.** The Connect listener starts a cycle at most once a second (`MIN_CYCLE`), and waits `RETRY_AFTER` after a cycle in which every session failed (`pause_after`). Test: `sdk::connect::wallet::tests::the_listener_never_cycles_faster_than_its_minimum_interval`.
- **SA-127.** The Connect processing lock is per session, and the notice that a request waits for the player is sent after the session's lock is released (`Flow::Waiting` carries it out). Test: `handlers::connect_e2e_tests::a_stalled_application_holds_no_disconnect_of_its_session`.

**Round four (2026-10-20).** The SoFi locator scans and SA-81, under the owner's storage-junk ruling (resource bounds and streaming recognition) and the Connect authority and isolation approval, with the CI gates round three left red. Mutations are recorded in VERIFICATION_MATRIX.

- **What a candidate is, from its bytes (SA-85; storage §4, §7; SoFi §11, §13).** A candidate whose bytes fewer than three members return is `Seen`. It is not `Stored`, but its bytes are what is at the address, because the address binds them (`judge`, `Candidate::Seen`). Bytes that are no object under the locator are nothing, however few members hold them. Bytes that are the object, short of `Stored`, leave the scan undecided. The count of members answering that they hold nothing decides nothing: a candidate no member returns bytes for may be the object (Amendment A1, MR-STOR-0021). This replaces a rule written earlier in this round and never pushed, which decided a candidate was nothing once three members answered absent. That rule read members' answers as a verdict, which storage §4 forbids, and resembled the quorum fallback the owner rejected. Tests: `sofi::storage::tests::bytes_seen_that_are_no_object_under_the_locator_are_nothing`, `::an_object_seen_short_of_stored_is_never_none`; `sdk::storage_io::tests::junk_one_member_holds_leaves_the_scan_complete`, `::an_object_fewer_than_three_members_hold_is_not_established`. Lean: `DSMSofiStorage.bytes_seen_that_are_no_object_under_the_locator_are_nothing`, `an_object_seen_short_of_stored_is_never_none`.
- **A member appends only what it holds (MR-SOFI-0096; storage §7, SoFi §11: "Anyone MAY append the content address of an object the member already holds").** The node used to append any 32 bytes. It now appends an address only when it holds the immutable object there, and otherwise answers 422 (`api::cells::append_index`, `db::holds_immutable_object`). It reads nothing of the object. MR-SOFI-0096 had been recorded Met without this conjunct. Test: `dsm_storage_node::cells_keep_everything::an_address_the_member_holds_no_object_at_is_not_appended`. A hostile member can still list an address it does not hold, and such a candidate stays not established. The MR-STOR-0021 tests model that member by writing to one node's store directly (`test_support::nodes::NodeSet::list_unheld`): `sdk::sofi_flow::tests::a_setup_scan_that_met_an_unestablished_candidate_is_not_a_refusal`, `sdk::sofi_reads::tests::an_unestablished_genesis_candidate_is_not_read_as_unpublished`.
- **SA-130: what an index read covers.** A read covers the locator only when at least `members − STORAGE_FINALITY_COUNT + 1` members read their index to its end (`Coverage`, `IndexEnd`). With fewer, an object published under the locator may be among no candidate, so the scan is never None or Complete. Tests: `sofi::storage::tests::a_read_too_few_members_ended_is_never_none`; Lean `a_read_too_few_members_ended_is_never_none`.
- **SA-88: candidates merged by rank.** `merge_index_reads` takes each member's n-th address before any member's (n+1)-th, once each, so one member's fabricated addresses take only their share of a scan's budget. Tests: `sofi::storage::tests::index_reads_interleave_by_rank_so_no_member_starves_another`, `::index_reads_merge_by_rank_then_member_without_duplicates`.
- **SA-87, SA-89, SA-132: a flood at a predictable locator is read once.** A scan moves each member's cursor through the leading run of entries whose bytes it read (`remember_passed_over`). The run's recognized addresses are kept, and every later scan examines them again first. The cursors and addresses live in `final_reads::PassedOver`, per set, namespace and locator, held to `CURSOR_BUDGET`. The next scan reads each member on from its cursor (`SetClient::read_index_after`). Junk written before or after the objects it hides therefore costs a process its reads once. An entry no member returns bytes for stops the run, so nothing undecided is skipped. The record is process memory and nothing is persisted, so a fresh process pays for the flood once more. SA-87: a history-leaf read that is not complete is `BelowBaseline::LeavesNotEstablished`, not `NotProven`. SA-132: under the baseline locator, only a baseline Core authenticates as the owner's is recognized (`recognize_owners`). Two authenticated frontiers are an equivocation however much is unread, and one is adopted only from a complete read. Tests: `sdk::storage_io::tests::a_flood_past_the_budget_is_read_past_by_the_next_scan`, `::a_flood_after_the_object_is_read_past_by_the_next_scan`; `handlers::node_e2e_tests::baseline_shaped_junk_behind_the_owners_baseline_is_read_past`.
- **SA-81.** An accept for a session the application already holds is answered from what it holds, before any signature is checked or the wallet's directory is read. The same bytes again are that session. Other bytes are refused ("this session holds another accept"), as the store already refused them after verification. Test: `handlers::connect_e2e_tests::a_replayed_accept_is_answered_before_it_is_verified`.
- **A fixture rebuilt.** `handlers::node_e2e_tests::nothing_but_the_leaders_first_fulfillment_decides_k_ful` built its "precommit nobody can read" from junk bytes that one member held. Junk is now decided nothing, so the fixture is a precommit B signed that one member alone holds: it is the precommit, and never Stored.
- **CI on round three.** The clockless gate (`ci/no_clock_and_no_json.sh`) found `Instant::now` in two places round three added. The SA-82 listener now runs each cycle beside a `MIN_CYCLE` pause (`tokio::join!`), so it reads no clock, and SA-109's test asserts the verdict without timing it. CodeQL found a test panic message that printed an ingest reason derived from a public key (`handlers::recipient_dispatch` tests); the message no longer prints it. The SPHINCS source map was regenerated: line numbers and one blob moved, and no binding changed.

**Round five (2026-10-22, `fix/security-audit-open-rows`).** The approved rows of "Open, next" that tests settle without a further owner decision, and the Coverage run `main` has failed since #1142. Each fix has a test that performs what it refuses; the mutations, one `DSM_MUTANT` build in a scratch worktree with a clean control beside them, are recorded in VERIFICATION_MATRIX.
- **SA-69: a checkpoint names cells only once eligible.** Anyone may append a checkpoint naming any 33 roots, and every root a walk is handed is a cell it reads. Discovery keeps a checkpoint aside, and its roots become candidates only when it is eligible at a head this device's own walks established (`Candidates::admit_checkpoints`, `CheckpointV1::eligible_at`; SoFi S23, "a fresh reader", step 2), in the reserve walk and the vault walk alike. One walk reads ahead at most `NAMED_READS_PER_WALK` named roots, one for each generation a discovery reads, the most an honest index names (`Candidates::named_from`); past it the walk reads each cell when it reaches it. A checkpoint anyone appended for a segment's start no longer stops this device owing the segment's own (`owe_checkpoint` compares the checkpoint it would publish). Tests: `sdk::lineage_discovery::tests::a_checkpoint_names_roots_only_once_eligible_at_an_established_head`, `::a_walk_reads_ahead_no_more_named_roots_than_its_bound`, `::only_the_segments_own_checkpoint_stands_for_its_debt`; `handlers::faucet_flow_tests::a_checkpoint_no_walk_established_names_no_cell_the_walk_reads` (no cell of a root only the checkpoint named is asked of any member).
- **SA-75: the walk holds one release at a time.** The generation chain a walk owes hints and checkpoints from was built from every memoised release since `R_0`, loaded at once under the database lock. It is now folded one row at a time (`fold_memoised_lineage`): each release's evidence address is taken and the release let go before the next is read. `memoised_lineage` is gone. No stored format changes: an earlier version of this round stored the digest in a new column, which needed client DB schema 33, and a schema bump makes every install refuse its database until it is wiped whole, every table included (the device head with its offline account, pending admissions, peer frontiers, anchor roots and enrollments, spent nonces, bilateral sessions, the sender outbox). The step digest needs no column, so none was added; the schema bump to 33 this round makes is for SA-141 and SA-143, under the owner's rule (2026-10-23): "we don't keep legacy code ... There's no migration ... We replace." Test: `sdk::native_reserve::tests::the_generation_chain_is_the_memoised_releases_up_to_the_first_gap`. Not mutation-proven: holding one release instead of the list is not observable in a test. Not done: the memo still keeps every release since `R_0`, since `release_at` answers verifiers from it; how much of it a device keeps is a retention decision.
- **SA-76: reads made ahead share a byte window.** The reads a walk makes together, the named roots' cells and the lookahead, share one `route_seats::ReadWindow` of `READ_AHEAD_BYTES`, the size of the final-cell cache their finals go to. A seat whose kept copies would pass the window is not read, as a seat past its own budget is not (a resource limit, never a verdict); a log is never read with copies left out, and what a dropped log took is given back. The walk reads such a cell itself when it reaches it. Test: `sdk::route_seats::tests::reads_made_together_keep_no_more_than_their_window`. The reserve wiring is covered by the faucet and vault-history suites; it is not mutation-proven separately.
- **SA-144: history amounts travel whole.** `TransactionInfo` carries its magnitude (`amount`) with an `AmountDirection` (field 19), and `TokenMove` carries `amount` and `direction` (5, 6); the signed fields (9; 3) are reserved. A row of 2^63 base units or more is reported, and no longer fails the whole history (SA-52's refusal by name, which `history_refuses_an_amount_beyond_the_signed_range` pinned). The frontend signs the domain amount from the direction and refuses a transfer or a moved token that names none. Tests: `handlers::wallet_routes::history_tests::history_reports_amounts_beyond_the_signed_range_whole`; frontend `mappers.test.ts` "carries an amount past the signed range whole, signed by its direction" and "refuses a transfer or a moved token that names no direction".
- **SA-147: a contact's row is its whole device id.** The directory add keyed a contact by 40 bits of a hash of its device id; every other path already keys it by the whole id, and now this one does (`contact_id_of`). Test: `sdk::contact_sdk::tests::a_contacts_row_id_is_its_whole_device_id`.
- **Coverage on `main` since #1142: the wallet overflows its stack in the unoptimized build.** `crates/dsm-app-host/tests/real_connection.rs` timed out at its first Connect request because the wallet process aborted with `thread 'dsm-sdk-runtime' has overflowed its stack` (macOS crash reports of two runs). The crashed thread is 80 frames, 76 distinct; the only frames that repeat (at most three times) are boxed-future and `catch_unwind` glue, so there is no recursion. Its frames sum to about 2.2 MB against tokio's 2 MiB worker stack; the largest, read from the debug binary's prologues, are the router's `invoke` dispatch (540 KB), `sync_session` (309 KB), `execute` (289 KB, twice), `process` (208 KB) and `handle_connect_invoke` (185 KB). In the release build the board and the phones run, the same path is about 0.3 MB. AcceptIssued also entered the router a second time to root its object; it now calls the adoption directly (`AppRouterImpl::add_by_anchor`, `65fcdc6b`). The Coverage workflow's Rust step sets `RUST_MIN_STACK=8388608` (`301c252b`), which the SDK runtime's workers inherit (it sets no stack size) along with the host processes the test starts; with it the Coverage-profile run passed whole locally (282 s). Production stacks are unchanged.
- **SA-71: a prepared fulfillment is completed, never a second signed.** Owner, 2026-10-23: "complete the existing fulfillment and never sign a second, different fulfillment at the same position"; "Once a fulfillment is durably prepared, retry that exact fulfillment rather than creating another"; "If conflicting claims already exist, respect the canonical storage result"; "If the state cannot be reconciled consistently, fail closed rather than inventing a recovery path." A trader signed `F`, published it and only then advanced its head, so a trader stopped in between held no record of `F` and signed a second at the same position. `F`'s objects are now frozen with their signatures, bound to the parent position and root, before any is published (`prepare_fulfillment`, purpose `sofi-prepared-fulfillment/<position>` in `frozen_publication_artifact`, no schema change). The position is part of the key because a root repeats: a Void position keeps its parent's root, and the first version, keyed by root alone, picked up the fulfillment prepared one position earlier (`a_trade_that_loses_its_key_to_another_resolves_void_and_the_next_realizes` went red on it). A trade, route or close that finds a fulfillment frozen against its parent completes that one and is not carried out itself (`exercise_draft_at_head`). Frozen objects that do not read back as one fulfillment of one precommit on that parent are refused, and nothing is signed or completed (`prepared_fulfillment`). A position that already holds another fulfillment than the pending one keeps failing closed at resolution (`resolve_pending_position`). Test: `handlers::node_e2e_tests::a_fulfillment_prepared_and_published_is_completed_never_signed_again` (stopped after publication through `draft_trade` and `prepare_fulfillment`; the next trade completes the prepared fulfillment, the position registers it, and only its balances move).
- **SA-104, SA-145: the built-in tickers are reserved.** Owner, 2026-10-23: reserve ERA and dBTC, provided "the existing CPTA commitment remains the authoritative asset identity" and "financial operations use the CPTA policy commitment, not merely the ticker". Checked in source, not by mutation: an online send (`wallet.sendSmart`, `wallet.sendOffline`) resolves the sender's own ticker to a commit, and the signed operation carries that commit; the BLE receiver resolves the peer's ticker and refuses the step unless it is the commit the operation signs (`bilateral_ble_handler` receiver confirm); a received online transfer is credited by its commit (§6.85); a Connect payment names its commit (§6.85); the bilateral settlement's own resolution feeds only the projection and history rows written after the advance. What a ticker still decided was which local row and label a token got. Creation and adoption now share one rule (`token_routes::ticker_refusal`): 2 to 8 characters (SoFi §47), never a built-in ticker in any letter case (`core::token::BUILTIN_TICKERS`); `adoptable_policy` applies it, so every path that roots a policy does. SA-103 is not fixed by the reservation.
- **SA-103: a ticker is any 2 to 8 characters.** Owner, 2026-10-23: "Keep §47: any 2 to 8 characters. Make balance.list show non-ASCII tickers instead of refusing them." `balance.list` refused a held token whose ticker was not printable ASCII, and with it the whole list; it now refuses only a balance key that names no token. The one ticker normaliser (`wallet_routes::canonicalize_token_id`; the copy in `sdk::token_state` is removed) keeps any ticker but a built-in's exactly, spaces included, so the registry finds it. Found on the way: Core's policy parser counted the ticker in bytes, so a five-letter ticker of ten bytes, which §47 and `token.check` allow, failed at `token.create`; it now counts characters (`economic::token_policy`). Tests: `handlers::balance_list_tests::a_held_token_whose_ticker_is_not_ascii_is_listed_as_it_is`, `handlers::wallet_routes::tests::canonicalize_token_id_keeps_any_other_ticker_exactly`, `dsm::economic::token_policy::tests::a_ticker_is_counted_in_characters_not_bytes`. Test: `handlers::token_routes::tests::a_ticker_naming_a_builtin_is_neither_adopted_nor_created`. A wallet that adopted such a coin before this build keeps it; nothing is reset. SA-148 (`token.forget` residue) is not addressed by the rule and stays open.

Adoption is permanent; delete the route and its code and tests." `token.forget` deleted the registry row and the cached policy and left the adoption leaf and the projection row, so the issuer could keep crediting a token the device no longer named. **Owner rulings on the design questions, 2026-10-18.** The owner's review of the ten questions, in its words where they decide something:
- Offline bearer: "Approve root tracking as an additional physical-continuity guard. Do not treat it as a complete solution to offline allocation forgery. Disable the vulnerable acceptance path until the complete proof is implemented."
- Storage junk: "Approve resource bounds and streaming recognition. Reject quorum fallback and an unconditional per-key write cap. Keep nodes as byte-storage operators, not transaction authorities."
- Faucet: "Do not approve the proposed faucet changes as sufficient. Fix release entitlement, predecessor binding, candidate recognition and bounded reserve walks together."
- SoFi liveness: "Approve SA-72, SA-83, SA-86 and SA-131 as implementation corrections consistent with the existing predicates. Approve SA-71 only after resolving the §25 crash/discard semantics."
- Economic verifier: approved with conditions (Core authoritative over every SDK cache; incomplete evidence is never acceptance or invalidity; a frozen witness must prove an accepted sender state; a conditional predecessor yields only its selected root).
- Recovery: "Approve the verification-order change immediately."
- Connect: "Approve the authority and isolation changes. Redesign stake withdrawal around independently verifiable settlement or challenge evidence."
- Token schema: "Approve the schema bump and reset in beta, with recovery/reprovision tests", on the condition that a reset never "silently destroy[s] unrecoverable economic state, offline bearer state, recovery material or pending transfer evidence."
- Hardware: "Approve the provisioning architecture, but do not perform irreversible operations on the deployed hardware until the replacement authentication path and boot chain are verified."
- Proceed now: "SA-72, SA-73 verification ordering, SA-83, SA-86, SA-92, SA-95, SA-117 verifier correction, SA-121 and SA-131, along with straightforward bounds and fail-closed validation changes." Then, 2026-10-18: "Need to go check things for yourself... Make the corrections."

**What the specs say, checked against the rulings.**
- Storage spec §9, finality rules 4 and 5: "If the leader is unreachable, the cell waits. No other member stands in." Three links "are not a quorum and do not vote." A seat-quorum fallback is excluded.
- Storage spec §9, route-chain rule 3: "Bytes that are not a recognized object naming `K` never count, so junk written to the leader blocks nothing." The SDK's whole-cell byte budget (SA-67, and SA-62 at the reserve cell) refuses a leader's log on bytes that never count, so it is a conformance violation of rule 3, not an open design question. The fix is the ruled streaming recognition.
- SoFi §25: "F signed, never published: not exercised; the trader may discard it", and "F held by members, but not by the leader of Kful(q): not exercised; a different F at the leader wins q." Signing once per position would contradict §25. SA-71 is fixed within §25: when another of the device's own fulfillments holds the leader of `Kful(q)`, resolution follows that fulfillment instead of refusing for good.
- DSM §70: "Transfer uniqueness, offline included, is a software theorem of the guarded linear kernel ... It holds with the anchor hardware deleted." A receiver that credits a sender-chosen allocation pre-state (SA-61) breaks that theorem in the implementation; pinning roots in the appliance would make hardware the uniqueness authority §70 rejects. SA-61 is a gap between §52/§67's predicate and the receiver's check, and the vulnerable acceptance path is to be disabled until the predicate is complete.

**Open, for the owner.** These change protocol design or contradict a claim the specs make, and wait on the questions put to the owner with this record: offline bearer anchoring (SA-61, SA-91, SA-112, SA-116); junk under predictable keys and fixed read budgets (SA-62, SA-67, SA-85, SA-87, SA-88, SA-89, SA-97, SA-99, SA-130, SA-132); reserve releases by self-made identities (SA-63) and how much of the reserve memo a device keeps (SA-75); economic verifier rules (SA-93, SA-94, SA-133 to SA-136; SA-95's selected-root condition against A14's one-hop bound; SA-92's persisted vault-chain rows); old-device invalidation beyond the verifier (SA-117: refusing a tombstoned device's messages); the offline bearer proof that would re-enable receipt (SA-61); Connect authority, pacing and privacy (SA-77 to SA-82, SA-102, SA-127, SA-140); the hardware anchor (SA-74). SA-149 is dBTC's and out of scope.

### 6.90 A payer paid out of a root it invented: acceptance adjacent to the receiver's own frontier (`fix/security-audit-2026-10-18`, DSM Amendment A19, SA-02, 2026-10-20)

**The finding (SA-02, §6.84).** Under A14 a receiver validated a peer's step from the root the step's own witness was built on (`parent_named_by`), and never read the claim at the position before. A claim is self-signed and the register keeps the first claim written, so nothing checked where that root came from. A payer's software could build a valid step on a root it invented, register one claim on it, and be paid by a receiver that held nothing of it. Fork detection catches two claims, not one invented one, and A14's boundary (exposure at reconciliation) cost a throwaway identity nothing. §6.68 had closed this attack before A14.

**Owner ruling (2026-10-20, quoted in DSM Amendment A19).** The owner first stated that there are no strangers: every counterparty is a contact added online (Amendment A3). On the check: "Supposed to be checked against the storage nodes." On the receiver's cost: "Why wouldn't you just recache with the update? … every time there's a new one, you recache and then you still only have one step each new time." Then: "Get cracking." No DSM object is a validity fact a device cannot forge (claims, signatures and receipts are self-made, and an anchor measurement would make hardware the authority §70 rejects), so the one fact a receiver can hold without a ledger is a coordinate it validated itself. A19 restores A8 for acceptance on that basis. Transferable validity proofs, which would make the cost constant without the cache, are named as the later replacement and are not built.

**What changed.**
- Core (`dsm::economic::peer_lineage`). `validate_peer_lineage` walks a peer from the receiver's frontier for it (`PeerFrontiers::frontier_below`), or its activation root, to the target. Each position's claim is read only at the cell routed from the root validated at the position before (`Verifier::final_claim`), and its step is validated from that root by `advance_validated`, which refuses a witness built on any other root. A credit's source is validated the same way, from the receiver's frontier for the source (`Verifier::source_step`), and every frontier the walk established (the target's, the position before it, each source's) comes back with the result (`Checked::reached`). `validate_peer_prefix` validates toward the head the register holds: it stops at an empty cell (`PrefixStop::Head`), or short, at a cell not decided yet or at the budget (`PrefixStop::Short`), and returns the frontier its validated segment reached. Past `WALK_STEP_BUDGET` steps a walk is `Incomplete` and reads nothing more. Each walk counts what it did (`StepCost`). A14's register-key probe, its rival weighing and its conditional-parent ladder (`register_key_values`, `located`, `probed`, `parents_of_conditional`) are deleted.
- SDK. The frontier store is `peer_frontier`, created if absent (client schema 32), read through `StoredFrontiers` (`economic_lineage::frontier_below`). Every walk's entry point (`resolve_peer`, `resolve_peer_root`, `resolve_peer_claim`, `resolve_peer_prefix`) records the frontiers it established in one transaction (`economic_registers::record_established`, `economic_lineage::record_frontiers`), whether the walk was an acceptance, a SetupValid read, a holdings check, a SoFi trader's root or a contact add. A walk that fails returns none, so nothing is recorded from it. A contact add starts a validation of the contact's lineage (`contacts_routes::prevalidate_contact_lineage`, `economic_registers::prevalidate_contact`); the add does not wait for it. The position before an acceptance's target is recorded too, so the walk that finishes the admission after commit starts from it. Each walk logs its cost under `[A19]`.
- `handlers::one_hop_verification_tests` is now `handlers::frontier_verification_tests`.

**Found on the way: a refused extension entry unmarked the running one.** The SDK suite's first run under A19 aborted: `handlers::node_e2e_tests::a_reader_at_a_baseline_proves_roots_below_it_from_the_vaults_history` overflowed its stack. A vault's chain is extended at most once per thread at a time (`sofi::resolve::Extending`): a judgement inside the extension that asks for the same chain is answered from what is recorded. `Extending::enter` built its guard with `bool::then_some`, which evaluates its argument either way, so a refused entry built a guard and dropped it at once, and the drop removed the vault from the set while the extension that marked it was still running. A walk of a trader whose positions each resolve through the vault nests three entries deep, which A14's one-hop reads never did; the third found the vault unmarked and extended the chain again, without end. The guard is now built only when the entry marked the vault (`then`). Test: `sofi::resolve::tests::a_refused_entry_leaves_the_running_extension_marked`; the overflowing test passes.

**SA-95 and SA-135.** Both were A14 mechanisms. SA-95: a conditional claim at n took either root of a conditional claim at n − 1 as its parent, so an honest back-to-back trade could look like a fork. Under A19 the parent is the one root the receiver resolved at n − 1. SA-135: the register probe and the lone-survivor rule are gone with discovery; a position is read at one routed cell.

**Open.**
- Transferable validity proofs (the owner's later replacement for the cache) are not built.
- A receiver new to an identity with a long history pays that history's walk once, at the add, in budgeted calls. A payment that arrives before the add's validation finishes walks from wherever the store stands. That is correct but slower.
- **Adversarial plan R01 to R08 (pasted 2026-10-21), against the 23 credit-source mutants.** Passed, new or strengthened: R05 and R06 (`frontier_verification_tests`), R01 (`recipient_admission_tests::an_outage_holds_the_transfer_cleanly_and_it_recovers`, whose own doc claimed "no frontier" and asserted none). Covered by named tests that already exist: R03 (policy re-hash, creator, exact supply), the reserve rows of R02 (generation zero, recipient, successor, foreign set, binding, evidence address), `consumed_leaf_required` of R04. **Not covered, no named test fails when the check is removed, and not written here because authoring them was blocked by the session's safety filter:** `asset_eq`, `dup_source`, `consumed_from_zero`, `consumer_op_id`, `debit_addressed_to_consumer`, `debit_is_op_debit`, `witness_matches_validated_root`, `acceptance_bundle_addr`, `acceptance_verified`, the reserve `reserve_coordinates` check (R02's wrong-generation case), and `source_may_name_sources`. R04's replayed-debit case rests on two of them. **Not run:** R07, because nothing constructs the `ResolvedSofi` arm it would exercise (`provenance.rs:103`); R08, because crash injection at persistence boundaries needs a failpoint in production code, which the plan forbids adding; the plan's differential test. Its original side does not exist in the tree: the balance map was hashed into every relationship tip until `a30f1215` (2026-08-27), when `relationship_chain_tip_v2` replaced it, and R_econ's primitives had landed three days earlier (`773cd0ec`), so that form was already two-authority; the specification's own form (§9, §30: a balance leaf under `ρcore`, `u` and Σ inside it) was never built, and the bilateral acceptance code never read the old `balance_witness`. A faithful reconstruction is blocked on four predicates the specification does not state: where a sender's pre-state balances come from absent history; the funding-source rule for a credit; how `u` and Σ enter `ρcore`; and how deep the "signed root chain" the receiver verifies at relationship creation (§9) goes and whether it checks transitions or only signatures. The scenarios that fabricate, replay or fork value (D01, D03, D04, D07, D08, D13) were not authored here: the session's safety filter blocks that class.
- **Measured cost of the current verifier (in-process harness with local storage nodes, not phones; plan Phase 5, one-sided because the original verifier cannot be run).** `acceptance_cost_follows_the_unseen_history_and_warm_costs_one_position`, payer with 0 / 1 / 10 / 100 payments to a third device the receiver never saw. Cold acceptance validates every unseen position: 2 / 3 / 12 / 103 positions, 3 / 4 / 13 / 104 cell reads, 0.73 / 0.75 / 1.0 / 3.8 s, so the cost grows linearly with unseen history (about 30 ms a position here) and is bounded by the 512-position walk budget. The next payment validates 1 position (2 reads, about 0.65 s, mostly fixed admission work whatever the history), and a second look at an accepted position 1 position (1 read, about 25 ms). The cache avoids repeating completed walks; it does not remove the first one. 1,000 and 10,000 positions were not run.
- **The receiver-side balance bound: specification, formal model, code (source review, 2026-10-21; no attack was run against `b7abd669`; this is a source-review finding, not a demonstrated exploit).**
  - *Specification.* §12 lists a resource-consumption proof among what a verifier receives, and "Verify resource key is unconsumed" in the acceptance path. §43 derives the key `κres(s, x)` from the parent's `ρcore`. §46 and §47 make the consumed set Σ an authenticated sparse map in which `K ∉ Σ` is provable. §9's example has the receiver see, against the presented parent, "the balance leaf reads 10, and `Kbal ∉ Σ0`". §9 and Amendment A4 say the payer's state is authenticated by its signed root chain; Amendment A8 (2026-09-30) says an authenticated root and a valid transition are "different facts", so a signed root chain alone does not establish that a root's balances came from valid transitions.
  - *Formal model.* `lean4/DSMRecognition.lean` has `Conserves s o := o.amount ≤ s.balance o.lineage` (line 277), makes it a conjunct of `Recognized` (line 302) beside consumed-key exclusion, and proves `overdraft_is_not_recognized` (line 459), with the bound's removal listed as mutation control 7. Read as written; Lean was not re-run for this note. It takes `s.balance` as "the state the reader holds" and does not say how a reader comes to hold the balance of a peer's lineage.
  - *Code at `b7abd669`.* Every balance invariant found runs on the executing device's own balances: `apply_token_balance_delta`, `verify_token_balance_consistency`, `DeviceState`'s `validate_conservation`, and the token SDK's `validate_token_conservation` (an error-recovery path over local caches). The receiver checked that its own credit equals the signed amount, the sender's signature, the pinned parent, replay and the receipt's relationship-leaf path. The device SMT held relationship tips; there was no balance leaf under the device root, and neither that tree nor the current one derives `κres` or holds Σ as a map in production code (the only such code is the paper's reference model, `tools/dsm_guarded_reference`).
  - *Classification.* An implementation omission relative to the specification's proof objects (a balance leaf under `ρcore`, `κres`, Σ), not shown to be a flaw in the design. The current code meets the receiver-side bound another way: `R_econ`, the register, consumed-source leaves and the frontier-relative walk (A8, A19).
  - *Open.* How a reader's `s` for a peer's lineage becomes trustworthy, which is the gap between a signed root chain and a chain of valid transitions; whether the specification's own form, with `R_econ` nested under `ρcore`, could supply it with less historical work is not settled. Offline: whether offline acceptance enforces sufficient authenticated value and single consumption without replay is not verified here; offline is out of scope this round except as a dependency boundary. No production code was changed on the strength of this finding.
- **The storage nodes in the online balance path (source review, 2026-10-21; DSM explainer §9, §11 and Amendments A2, A3, A4, A6, A7; storage specification §§1 to 5, 8, 9, 14, 22, 24. Nothing here was executed against the nodes.)**
  - *What the specification gives a receiver.* Exactly three storage facts, derived by Core from raw reads: `LeaderHeld`, `Final` (the leader link and two further valid links on one route chain) and `Stored(o)` (three members return the exact bytes) (storage §4, §5, §9). At most one value holds a cell's leader link, so at most one root claim is final at each `(G, DevID, position)` (storage §22.7). That is uniqueness and memory. "Registered is not Validated, and a storage fact implies nothing about semantic validity" (storage §4); nothing a node returns is a verdict; a node "MUST NOT gain authority from the bytes it stores" (§2) and never computes a balance (§1).
  - *So the register cannot stand in for the walk.* A device can register a self-consistent claim on a root no valid transition produced, and the cell holds it as final (explainer §11: "Registered is not validated"). That was the mechanism of SA-02, closed by A19. What the receiver does against the nodes is: read the cell routed from the root it validated before, derive `Final` from the reads, fetch the claim's evidence by content address and re-hash it, and recompute the transition itself.
  - *Order and cost.* A transition that is Invalid on what the verifier already holds never causes a storage read (storage §9.3, A4). A route link becomes checkable only once the ByteCommit that commits it has closed (§9.7, §14). Every cost measured in this section is node reads: a cold acceptance reads each unseen position's cell once, plus the evidence objects; the frontier removes repeats and does not remove the first walk.
  - *Failure.* An unreachable leader, or two of a route's further seats, is a liveness failure and the cell waits (storage §3, §9.4). The result is "not established" (`Incomplete`), never `Invalid` and never `Accepted`, and nothing negative is recorded (§4).
  - *Assumption inherited by any design that uses the register.* A member never alters, reorders or loses what it holds for a key, including across restore from a snapshot (storage §3.2 and §3.3). Combined commitment or walk, the anti-equivocation of two counterparties rests on it.
  - *Where confidentiality is specified.* The spool is sealed end to end (A7, storage §8.2) and the tip mirror's per-relationship leaves are encrypted (§8.1). Immutable objects carry no confidentiality property (§5): their payloads are opaque to the node, not secret from a reader. The implementation publishes a relationship step's economic evidence (the witness with its balances, the successor evidence with the operation and counterparty, the authority evidence, the acceptance bundle) as immutable objects reachable from the public root claim; this is the read-only code map of `1efca633` and is not re-executed here, and G16 records the audit of what a transfer publishes as open. A walk over a third party's history reads those objects from the nodes.
  - *The old tree.* `economic/register.rs` is absent at `b7abd669`, so the nodes' register was not part of acceptance there; the explainer's §9 uses it for "the same balance, two counterparties". Whether another mechanism covered that case was not traced.
  - *Open in the storage specification, relevant here.* Item 1 (where the device register's committed set lives in device state) and item 15 (an ancestry accumulator over ByteCommits, which A15's phase C needs). "Mirror" is two things in that document, the tip mirror (§8.1) and the peers' mirror of ByteCommits (§14); they are not conflated above.
- The owner's direction to record every validated frontier, reads included, reached the session as pasted text on 2026-10-21. The owner confirmed it in their own words the same day: "treat the pasted 2026-10-21 frontier text as my direction for A19." Amendment A19 quotes it.
- The costs have not been measured on the phones. The costs §6.72 recorded for walking the game's account under A8 came from walks with no recorded frontier; an add now records one, and a phone run is owed.

**Suites (release, 2026-10-20).** `dsm` whole crate, lib and every integration binary, at this round's tree: 1774/0 in 21 binaries (lib 1526/0). `dsm_sdk` lib, the whole suite, at the guard fix: 1349 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored that predate this work. Its first run under A19 aborted at the stack overflow above. `dsm_sdk` integration binaries: 39/0 in 12. `handlers::frontier_verification_tests` with the two tests rebuilt below: 10/0. `make lint`'s Rust half (fmt and clippy, all targets) exit 0; its frontend half was not run here (no `node_modules` in this worktree, and nothing in the frontend changed). The real-code guard, the clockless gate, the flow and forbidden-symbol gates, `ci/bridge_rpc_names.py`, the four peer-lineage gates, the SPHINCS source map and `ci/conformance_evidence.py` pass.

**Mutations.** Each was run on a committed tree and restored byte for byte; the matrix records them. The parent rule: the claim read off the validated chain, and the step validated from the root its witness names (A14's parent), each turn a named test red; under the second, the replayed debit is validated a second time. The frontier: no sender frontier, and no source frontiers, recorded with the acceptance. The add: validating another identity than the contact. Reads: `resolve_peer` recording what it reached. The budget: never spent. The guard: `then_some`. Two tests were rebuilt because their mutations stayed green or went red for another reason. The SA-02 test first replayed a faucet claim, which the release's position binding refuses under either parent rule; it now replays a debit. The credit-source test's second payment carried no new credit from C, so it never needed C's frontier; C now pays A twice.
